'Is this a joke?': Centcom podcast mocked as Iran war drags on
articles.summary:
'Is this a joke?': Centcom podcast mocked as Iran war drags on

Submitted by Elis Gjevori on Fri, 11/06/2026 - 11:29
The US command drew widespread ridicule as its chief joked about French fries and said nothing about the Minab school strike which killed 120 children
Inside Centcom podcast with Admiral Brad Cooper (left) and Fleet Master Chief Lateef Compton (Screengrab/Centcom/YouTube)
Off

The Pentagon has entered its podcast bro era, and viewers have widely derided its debut.

As the cost of the US-Israeli war on Iran spirals for American taxpayers, US Central Command (Centcom) launched its official podcast on Thursday.

The first episode of Inside Centcom pairs Admiral Brad Cooper, who leads the US command overseeing the war, with Fleet Master Chief Lateef Compton.

In the 12-minute episode on YouTube, Cooper jokes about stealing French fries from Compton’s lunch. The pair touch only briefly on the deeply unpopular war, now in its ninth month. Centcom turned off comments on YouTube.

The podcast looks like an attempt to reach young men who might one day fight Washington’s wars in the Middle East.

"It's called service for a reason. You're going to give more than you're going to get. But if you find satisfaction in giving, you'll have no greater satisfaction than serving in the United States military in particular," claimed Cooper. 

"It’s been a busy year," Compton joked at the start of the episode, a passing nod to a war that has killed thousands in Iran and left the US mired in another Middle East conflict.

Cooper said nothing about the US strike on the Shajareh Tayyebeh primary school in Minab, southern Iran, on 28 February, the first day of the war.

IRGC turned these mfs into podcasters https://t.co/dJJdlVAckB

— BODEGA PEPTIDES (@bigsnugga) November 5, 2026

Amnesty International said the strike killed 156 people, including 120 children, and concluded that the US violated international humanitarian law by failing to take all feasible precautions to protect civilians.

UN human rights experts said in September that there were "reasonable grounds" to believe the US committed war crimes in Iran.

“For sure, no one could have imagined the trajectory of events that we would be on, but through it, everyone has been doing a fantastic job,” Cooper said.

'Shitshow'

On X, viewers were less forgiving. The clip drew more than two million views, and one user called it a “shitshow”.

“Is this a joke? Its completely undignified. The host should ask him for his reflections on killing 168 schoolchildren and teachers in Minab,” journalist Murtaza Hussain wrote.

“Why the fuck are top US military officials podcasting?” another user posted.

Thank you CENTCOM, we definitely needed this! I’m so excited for the second episode! Maybe they’ll get a good guest like Jake Paul or Nicki Minaj, ooo, or maybe even Netanyahu! https://t.co/3DRWZcCfF0

— OSINTdefender (@sentdefender) November 5, 2026

“Thank you CENTCOM, we definitely needed this! I’m so excited for the second episode! Maybe they’ll get a good guest like Jake Paul or Nicki Minaj, ooo, or maybe even Netanyahu!” another wrote.

Trita Parsi, a US-based expert on Iran, wrote on X: “I am all in favor of Centcom abandoning the needless-wars-in-the-Middle-East business and going all in on podcasting…”

CENTCOM is now doing Gen Z propaganda to attract younger audiences by doing these trendy podcasts.

Even the cuts and edit style is exactly like these freelancers’ podcasts lmao. What a sh*tshow. https://t.co/d4J0Sadm1B

— Arya Yadegaar (@AryJeayBackup) November 5, 2026

Christopher K Mellon, a former US deputy assistant secretary of defence for intelligence, was equally scathing.

“I’m sorry, the American public does not need to become personally familiar with the idiosyncrasies of our CENTCOM commander; the American people need our CENTCOM commander to execute his or her duties somberly, professionally, and excellently,” Mellon wrote.

I am all in favor of Centcom abandoning the needless-wars-in-the-Middle-East business and going all in on podcasting... https://t.co/BtaU3oP4eE

— Trita Parsi (@tparsi) November 6, 2026

Democratic congresswoman-elect Elaine Luria wrote on X that Cooper’s job “is to win wars, not record podcasts…read the room”.

The Pentagon’s latest estimate to Congress puts the cost of the war at $47.1bn. Brown University estimates that American consumers have paid more than $153bn in additional fuel costs.

articles.title: Mohammed Hijab suggests UK counter-terror police tried to recruit him as informant
articles.summary:
Mohammed Hijab suggests UK counter-terror police tried to recruit him as informant

Submitted by MEE staff on Fri, 11/06/2026 - 11:02
British YouTuber publishes image purportedly showing counter terrorism police saying he 'doesn't want to be an informant'
Mohammed Hijab speaks at the Oxford Union in late 2025 (Screengrab)
Off

Prominent British YouTuber Mohammed Hijab has claimed that counter-terrorism police tried to recruit him as an informant after seizing his devices.

Hijab, whose legal name is Mohamed Hegab, describes himself as a philosopher of religion pursuing a PhD in the subject at the University of Birmingham.

He has more than a million subscribers on YouTube and frequently takes parts in debates on religion, as well as political issues.

In a post on X on Wednesday, Hijab said: "I want this on the record.

"In May, counter terrorism police stopped me without explanation, seized my devices and read more than ten thousand messages. My phone came back on 11 September. No further questions."

Hijab added: "Their notes, disclosed through my subject access request. One line reads 'Doesn’t want to be an informant.'"

He posted a screenshot of a page marked "REDACTED EXCERPT - Unrelated content removed" which has the Counter Terrorism Policing (CTP) logo on it and the heading: "Examining Officer's Notes - Continued".

All the notes in the screenshot are redacted apart from a handwritten line which says: "Doesnt want to be an informant."

It is unclear whether the entire document was redacted by the police, or whether Hijab blacked it out himself to protect sensitive information.

I want this on the record. In May, counter terrorism police stopped me without explanation, seized my devices and read more than ten thousand messages. My phone came back on 11 September. No further questions. Their notes, disclosed through my subject access request. One line reads “Doesn’t want to be an informant.”

— Mohammed Hijab (@mohammed_hijab) November 4, 2026

Hijab shared a second screenshot of a letter purportedly from "Gatwick Borders Team", referring to Gatwick airport, which is part of Counter Terrorism Policing South East. 

The letter, dated 18 May, says: "Further to your examination under Schedule 7 of the Terrorism Act which was conducted at Gatwick airport on the 12th May 2025, I am writing to inform you of a change in power used to retain the property that was seized from you."

Two paragraphs below it are redacted. The letter then reads: "This does not necessarily mean you are currently under criminal investigation.

UK bans clothes designer over T-shirts criticising 'western cuck' support for Israel
Read More »

"We will endeavour to return your items to you at the earliest opportunity."

MEE contacted CTP London for comment but did not receive a response by the time of publication.

Schedule 7 of the Terrorism Act 2000 gives the police the power to detain and question people at airports without needing prior grounds to suspect them of terrorism.

Hijab said in a recent YouTube video: "I was recently called in for a police interview under caution. I wasn't arrested but it was a criminal investigation and still is one. And it's one that relates to, I would call it, obviously from my perspective, activism.

"The questions were essentially questions that were for the most part related to anti-Israeli activism, actually."

He said he believed Israel was trying to "interfere" with him. Hijab did not provide evidence for these claims.

Hijab has participated in public debates on Israel, including on broadcaster Piers Morgan's show. 

He recently debated Jonathan Conricus, a former international spokesperson for the Israeli military, on Morgan's show.

articles.title: Fake Iranian accounts ‘campaigned for Netanyahu’ ahead of Israeli election
articles.summary:
Fake Iranian accounts ‘campaigned for Netanyahu’ ahead of Israeli election

Submitted by MEE staff on Fri, 11/06/2026 - 11:17
Network of 1,653 X profiles reportedly pushed Israelis to back Likud in coordinated Hebrew posts, then went back to promoting the shah’s son
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu speaks following exit polls in Jerusalem on 28 October (Ronen Zvulun/Reuters)
Off

A network of 1,653 X accounts posing as Iranian users amplified Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s election campaign ahead of last week’s vote, Haaretz reported on Friday.

The accounts posted messages in Hebrew urging Israelis to vote for Netanyahu “on behalf of the Iranian people”.

The accounts, which claimed to belong to Iranians living in Iran or abroad, appeared to coordinate their activity. Their operators remain unidentified.

Activity intensified on election day, when multiple accounts published identical messages and responded to posts in coordinated bursts.

Two accounts, for example, shared 109 identical posts, compared with just four expected through organic activity, according to Haaretz’s analysis.

They also responded simultaneously, or within five minutes of each other, to 232 posts by 53 different accounts.

On election morning, two accounts posted the same Hebrew message about an hour apart: “We call on you to support Benjamin Netanyahu to finish the job”, accompanied by the hashtag #IsraeliElections2026.

“Tomorrow, vote only for the Likud party,” one account wrote in response to a Netanyahu post at 10pm on the eve of the election.

“Vote for Benjamin Netanyahu,” another posted twice within two minutes after midnight.

“Dear people of Israel, if you want to be protected from the Islamic Republic and the Axis of Resistance, vote,” read another message, published in Hebrew and English at around 2am.

Haaretz reported that the findings were based on research by Expose, a social media monitoring company that specialises in tracking digital influence operations and disinformation.

The investigation follows an earlier Haaretz report that found accounts previously linked to an influence campaign targeting Iran’s government had begun engaging with Israel’s election campaign and amplifying Netanyahu’s videos. 

Israel’s Netanyahu accused of attempting coup after election defeat
Read More »

The Brandeis Institute and FakeReporter subsequently filed a petition with the Central Elections Committee over the accounts identified in the investigation.

Expose found that around 1,600 of the accounts had been identified last year as part of an influence operation promoting Reza Pahlavi, the son of Iran’s last shah, who was overthrown in 1979, as an alternative to the Iranian government.

As Israel’s election campaign gathered pace in July, 185 of these accounts began interacting with Netanyahu’s social media profiles, including by sharing posts attacking his political opponents.

According to Haaretz, the network returned to its usual focus on Pahlavi after the election concluded last week.

Some of the findings were submitted to the Central Elections Committee in October as expert evidence in a petition brought by the Brandeis Institute and FakeReporter against Netanyahu, Likud and the Prime Minister’s Office.

The committee’s chairman, Judge Noam Solberg, rejected the petition on the eve of the election.

Solberg ruled that the network’s activity was subject to election advertising transparency requirements and appeared, on the face of it, to violate the law.

However, he said the committee could not reach a definitive ruling because the identities of those operating the accounts were unknown. He ordered the evidence to be referred to the police.

In response to the investigation published in October, the Prime Minister’s Office and Likud denied any connection to the accounts.

articles.title: Iran demands US action, says it will not accept commitments on paper
articles.summary:
Iran demands US action, says it will not accept commitments on paper

Iran will not rely on US commitments on paper as it considers entering a new diplomatic phase with Washington, Ali Baqeri, deputy secretary of Iran’s Supreme National Security Council, has said, according to Fars news agency. 

Referring to four rounds of negotiations over the past 18 months, Baqeri said Tehran believed the United States had derailed each round through hostile actions and breaches of commitments. 

“We must see practical actions on the part of the Americans,” he said, describing such steps as necessary before a new chapter in diplomacy could begin.

Baqeri also discussed Iran’s cooperation with Russia, saying a recent visit by Supreme National Security Council Secretary Mohsen Rezaei to Moscow was intended to convey a message from Iran’s leader to President Vladimir Putin.
